### ① Derived judgments

- **Face, right.** The committed tree is 4 files: `.changeset/29020-calendar-resize-without-end-field.md`, `ui/packages/plugin-calendar/src/CalendarView.tsx`, `ui/packages/plugin-calendar/src/ObjectCalendar.tsx` and one new test. None is under `packages/spec/src/**` and none is a governed surface (AGENTS.md Prime Directive #14). There is no `(narrowing)` arm. The review is owed by the `Clause-②: yes (widening)` line alone, so this is the declaration face at `TIER_DEFAULT`.
- **Public surface: `CalendarViewProps.endEditable?: boolean` (default `true`), right.** `CalendarViewProps` is re-exported from the package's only `exports` entry `.` (`src/index.tsx`, the `export type { CalendarViewProps, CalendarViewEvent } from './CalendarView'` line), so an optional member widens the published type. It is additive and optional, and its default keeps a standalone `CalendarView` host's behaviour unchanged. `MonthViewProps` and `TimeGridViewProps` gain a required `endEditable: boolean`, but neither is exported (the file's only exports are `CalendarViewEvent`, `CalendarViewProps`, `CalendarView` and the test-only `__resolveEventColorForTest`), so that change is internal.
- **The handle is gated on the declared field, right.** `ObjectCalendar` passes `endEditable={Boolean(calendarConfig.endDateField)}`. `calendarConfig` is `getCalendarConfig(schema)`, which reads the declared `calendar` block only (the `endField` alias is retired with a refusal, objectui#8355). It is the same `endDateField` that `handleEventDropDefault` uses to decide whether to write an end, so whether a handle is drawn and whether an end is written follow one source. At the head, every gesture that moves the end on its own is gated:
  - the month-view handle: `showResizeHandle = !!onEventDrop && endEditable && isSpanEnd`;
  - the month-view drop: a `resize-end` payload returns before `onEventDrop` when `!endEditable`;
  - the time-grid bottom handle: `onEventDrop && endEditable && entry.isEnd`.
  `handleEventPointerDown` sets `resize-bottom` only from that handle's `"bottom"` zone, and nothing else produces one. The top "Resize start" handle and the body move are left ungated on purpose (see ③). This matches the card's expected behaviour: no resize handle when the view declares no end field.
- **No new key; `Metadata-protocol: none`, right.** `endEditable` is a TypeScript component prop and not something an author can write in metadata:
  - `packages/spec` is untouched. `CalendarConfigSchema` stays a `strictObject` of the four keys `startDateField`, `endDateField`, `titleField` and `colorField`.
  - `@object-ui/types` is untouched.
  - `ObjectCalendar` computes the prop from the existing `endDateField` and never reads it from the schema.
  - `calendar-view-renderer.tsx` forwards a closed set of `CalendarViewProps` keys with no raw spread, so an authored `calendar-view` node cannot set the prop either.
  At the head, `git grep endEditable` outside the tests hits only `CalendarView.tsx`, `ObjectCalendar.tsx` and the changeset. No key, accepted value or metadata type is added, so this is not a protocol addition.
- **Accept set: the no-op drop guard, right, and not a surface change.** `sameInstant` and the early return in `handleEventDropDefault` stop the default handler from writing when the start it would write, and any end it would write, already equal the record's values read through `toDisplayDate`. An empty or unparseable stored value never matches, so a drop onto an empty date still writes. A host's own `onEventDrop` is not affected. It narrows no published input: it removes a write of unchanged values, which is the card's actual defect (`updated_at` bumps and after-update triggers fire).
- **Gates.** All 57 check-runs on this head are complete: 46 success, 11 skipped, 0 failed, 0 pending. These include `Check Changeset`, `Type Check UI`, `Test UI` (1/16 through 16/16), `Lint UI`, `Build & E2E UI` and `Governed Surface Queue Guard`.

### ② Semver level

- `Clause-②: yes (widening)` and `Metadata-protocol: none` each start their own line, in both the PR body and the changeset body. Both are right: the optional exported prop widens the public surface, and no metadata author can write anything new.
- The changeset is `'@object-ui/plugin-calendar': patch`, which is right. AGENTS.md's Post-Task Checklist step 3 sets the level by the protocol kind alone: kind `none` takes `patch`, and "a non-protocol change, widening or breaking, ships `patch`". Nothing is breaking, so no BREAKING banner, migration or ADR-0087 marker is owed. `Check Changeset` passed on this head.

### ③ Boundary flags

- `open_questions` is `[]` in the dev's `os-dev-report` (6572431153). There is nothing to answer.
- Out-of-scope finding 1, answered. With no end field, the time-grid top "Resize start" handle still writes the dragged start, and the event is redrawn an hour long. This is a real write of a changed date, not the card's unchanged-value write, so leaving it outside this PR is right. It is carried by #29197 (open, `domain:ui`, p2).
- Out-of-scope finding 2, answered. `calendar-view-renderer.tsx` does not forward `endEditable`, so authored `calendar-view` nodes keep the default `true`. This is outside the claimed file surface, and the card concerns the object calendar view. Keeping it out is also what keeps the prop from being authorable here (see ①). It is carried by #29197, which itself requires "No new metadata key".
